newsitem.title: UK: BCCI liquidator's fees total $218.7 mln.
newsitem.headline: BCCI liquidator's fees total $218.7 mln.

text.p: A total of $218.7 million in fees has been paid to the liquidators of the collapsed Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI), a report prepared by them for the British Government revealed on Wednesday.

The liquidators, partners at international accountancy and consultancy firm Deloitte & Touche (formerly Touche Ross), were paid $15.1 million in the fifth year of the liquidation to January 15, 1997 which compared to 16 million the previous year.
Fees paid to the liquidator have decreased markedly in recent years as the emphasis of the liquidation has shifted more towards litigation rather than the initial investigation.
BCCI collapsed in 1991 with debts of more than $12 billion and has become the biggest fraud in banking history and the most complex liquidation ever undertaken.

Last month, former shipping tycoon Abbas Gokal received a 14-year jail sentence for his part in the affair and was later ordered to pay 2.94 million pounds in compensation which will go into the fund used to pay out dividends to creditors of the bank.
The liquidation looks set to go on for years with major outstanding claims against the auditors of BCCI, Price Waterhouse and Ernst & Young and the Bank of England still to be resolved.

Creditors have already received a 24.5 percent dividend which amounted to over $2 billion and the liquidators are confident that a further 10 percent will be paid by the end of the year or early in 1998.

The figures supplied by Deloitte & Touche to the British Department of Trade and Industry show that the liquidation has paid out $94.5 million in legal fees, $32.7 million in payroll and contract staff and $56 million on premises and office services.

The report says that the liquidators have set aside a total of $31.4 million as security for the cost of the defendants should the liquidators lose their action against the auditors of BCCI. The report says further payments may be required.
